set.body:
Objective:
Close the ntab-over-Frame phase with cross-platform workflow evidence, documentation, performance receipts, and a dependency audit proving that Frame remains general and ntab remains neuroimaging-specific.

Acceptance:
- One realistic in-memory workflow inspects a dynamic Frame, binds a named-tuple metadata schema, filters, groups by multiple keys, binds dense/sparse/ROI/surface/parcel features, resolves, reduces, compares, inspects receipts, and drills to contributors.
- A group-ntab example prepares effects-only and variance-aware second-level inputs and reconstructs typed supported outputs.
- Frame metadata operations are measured to prove they do not resolve feature payloads.
- Feature resolution batches by resource and preserves requested Frame row order.
- Reduction receipts record source feature identity, exact support fingerprint, reducer, missing policy, groups, selected rows, effective counts, allocations, and contributor lineage.
- Independent fixtures establish numerical and support correctness; cross-platform tests establish shared behavior; JVM-only IO tests remain isolated.
- build.sbt, module relations, READMEs, and examples show the one-way dependency from ntab to Frame and leaf adapters above both.
- No duplicated scalar column store, expression IR, optimizer, join, grouping, ordering, or generic source API remains in ntab.
- Frame core has no transitive ScalaFIM dependency, and optional frame-gale or frame-duckdb artifacts are not required for ntab.
- compileAll and testAll pass on the exact integrated tip, or any unrelated blocker is reported without overstating completion.
set.title: ntab 3: cross-platform Frame integration, workflow evidence, docs, and dependency audit
